idiom_name: sealed trait + case objects/case classes + exhaustive match
implementation_notes: Scala models the state set as a closed algebraic data type: a sealed trait with case objects for stateless states and case classes for states that carry data, matched in a transition function that returns the successor instead of mutating. This replaces the State/ConcreteState hierarchy, and the compiler warns when a match over the sealed hierarchy is not exhaustive (-Xfatal-warnings turns that into an error). Case objects are singletons, so shared stateless states and equality come for free; when the state must be persisted, serialize the case object's name or add an explicit stable code rather than the object graph.
code_sketch:
sealed trait Phase
case object Draft extends Phase
case class Published(version: Int) extends Phase

def next(phase: Phase): Phase = phase match {
  case Draft        => Published(1)
  case Published(v) => Published(v + 1)
}
pitfalls: A non-exhaustive match compiles with a warning and fails at runtime with MatchError; make exhaustiveness fatal in the build.
A sealed trait is only closed within its own file, so splitting states across files silently loses the guarantee - Scala 3 enums keep them together.
Case classes are immutable values: storing mutable collaborators inside a state breaks equality, hashing and sharing.
